signal: Unfortunately, the provided search findings do not include recent research on the efficacy of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing in treating Huntington's disease in human clinical trials. The findings primarily discuss the potential of CRISPR-Cas9, its application in mice, and its use in editing human embryos to confer resistance to HIV. However, based on the available information, it can be inferred that CRISPR-Cas9 has shown promise in reversing Huntington's disease in mice. This suggests that the technique may have potential therapeutic applications for the disease. Nevertheless, it is crucial to note that mouse models do not always translate to human efficacy, and further research is necessary to determine the safety and effectiveness of CRISPR-Cas9 in humans. Regarding human clinical trials, there is no information provided in the search findings. As of my last update, there were no published results from human clinical trials using CRISPR-Cas9 to treat Huntington's disease. It is essential to consult recent scientific literature and clinical trial registries, such as ClinicalTrials.gov, to obtain the most up-to-date information on ongoing or completed trials. In summary, while CRISPR-Cas9 has shown potential in preclinical studies, particularly in mouse models, there is currently no available information on its efficacy in human clinical trials for treating Huntington's disease. Further research is necessary to fully explore the therapeutic potential of CRISPR-Cas9 for this condition.
